lane: K3-H1 ASGT: antislope-scarp grain traces (self-assigned and pre-registered; IR-K3-LANE-01: the prompt's lane paragraph is missing)
hypothesis: Scarps that face UPHILL (against the 100 m regional slope), are coherent over >=300 m and parallel the local fault grain are tectonic; small antislope scarps visible only in 1 m lidar are what pre-lidar fault compilations miss, so they should mark uncatalogued faults.
mechanism: Normal faulting in the Basin and Range produces antithetic/synthetic scarps whose free face can oppose the topographic slope; erosion, deposition, terraces and shorelines produce downhill-facing risers. Facing polarity x grain compatibility x coherence is therefore a fault-specific geomorphic signature.
non_fault_mimic: Landslide and sackung headscarps (uphill-facing ridge-top scarps: relief veto), channel banks (cross-slope dominance), roads/berms (short, straight; grain/coherence down-weight), lake shorelines (downhill-facing: excluded).
